title: Renyi interpolation bridge for the modular shell
question: Can the modular-frequency weighted Kubo--Mori shell be represented as the integral of a symmetric Renyi interpolation, with the beta/2 midpoint and endpoint modular moments separated by exact convexity envelopes?
method: Use the actual-Q3 edge and square finite fixtures with all translated sites and bond terms, both term orders, both time signs, every prefix position and both history adjoints on the declared cutoffs.
Diagonalize each doubled bond generator, construct normalized Gibbs probabilities and center every moved Hermitian witness in the same bond-Gibbs state.
For each context evaluate G(s)=sum_ij |log(p_i)-log(p_j)| p_i^s p_j^(1-s)|X_ij|^2 at the endpoints, midpoint and quarter points, and compute the exact integral from |p_i-p_j|.
Check Hermitian endpoint symmetry, the convex chord and midpoint/integral envelopes, the logarithmic-mean identity and a 12-node Gauss--Legendre reconstruction.
Rebuild the same finite grid in a non-importing independent lane and formalize the scalar geometric-mean/chord envelopes in Lean R380.
finding: The primary lane passes 30,733/30,733 assertions and the non-importing independent lane passes 14/14 aggregate assertions over 2,560 all-prefix actual-Q3 contexts. The integrated verifier passes 69/69 and Lean R380 compiles. Primary and independent numerical fields agree within 1.554312234475219e-14. The largest endpoint modular moment is 2.15358381458932, the largest midpoint modular moment is 0.360525986123478, and the largest integrated modular shell is 0.7305484440673373 before the (2/beta) shell factor. The meaningful midpoint/integral ratio reaches 0.9594837421464463 and the integral/endpoint ratio reaches 0.9240035972845281. Convexity, symmetry and logarithmic-mean residuals remain at roundoff scale.
decision_reason: The exact finite interpolation proves that the beta/2 midpoint is a lower control channel, while the endpoint modular-frequency moment supplies the upper envelope needed for the full shell. The finite ratios show that midpoint control alone does not replace endpoint control. This is a route-local separation of analytic obligations, not a uniform estimate or a QFT promotion.

adversarial_review.check: Equal eigenvalues use the continuous arithmetic value and never divide by a zero logarithmic gap.
The shell retains |log(p_i)-log(p_j)| before integration; no sign is discarded in the interpolation.
All weights are evaluated in the Hamiltonian eigenbasis without commuting rho and X.
G(0) and G(1) use opposite eigenvalue weights and their equality is checked from Hermitian entries.
The midpoint is tested as a lower bound for the integral and the endpoint chord as an upper bound, separately.
The shell integral is computed exactly from |p_i-p_j|; quadrature is only a secondary reconstruction check.
Ratios omit only values below the declared finite tolerance so roundoff zeros cannot create a false diagnostic.
The endpoint moment remains parameter-dependent on the finite grid, so no cutoff or volume uniformity is inferred.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator, graph, spectrum, prefixes and interpolation without importing the primary audit.
No common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A conclusion is drawn.

next_action: Bound the endpoint modular-frequency moment on a Hamiltonian-derived common core, or prove a source-local substitute, before inserting the shell interpolation into the R-377 resolvent telescope.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Renyi/Kubo--Mori interpolation interface only. It does not prove source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, modular tails, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.
no_overclaim: R-380 isolates endpoint modular-moment debt; it is not a uniform theorem or a QFT closure.
